fields.meta_title: E-Signature Workflow That Chases Every Signer | Emergent
fields.meta_description: Build an e-signature workflow that can wait for one signer before the next, reminds anyone who goes quiet, and files the signed copy.
fields.h1: Build an E-Signature Workflow That Chases Every Signer
fields.hero_description: Get an e-signature workflow that sends each document to its signers in order and files the signed copy where it belongs.
fields.features_heading: What Has to Happen Between Send and Signed
fields.features_subheading: Emergent builds the signing app from your description: who signs, in what order, when reminders go out, and where signed copies go.
fields.feature_1:
Signer roles written as a brief

Describe who signs each document and in what order, as you would to a new office manager. Emergent builds the request form and the signer roles from that description.
fields.feature_2:
A signing page inside the app

The app Emergent builds can capture e-signatures on its own signing page. If your team already pays for a signing tool, the app connects to it through its API instead.
fields.feature_3:
Reminders that stop at the signature

Pick the days a signer who has not signed hears from you again. The app sends each reminder by email or Slack, and a signature cancels any reminder still waiting to go out.
fields.feature_4:
Signed copies filed for you

When the last signature lands, the app names the finished file your way and saves it where your team looks, such as a shared drive folder or the customer's record in your CRM.
fields.feature_5:
A live board of open requests

See which documents wait on whom and for how many days so far. The board updates live as signers open and sign, so nobody has to ask the sender where a document stands.
fields.feature_6:
A signing record you own

Each signature is stored with its time and the exact version that was signed, in a database you own. Pull it up the day a client asks which copy they agreed to and when.

fields.tab_content_1:
The agency signs only after Tamsin Orchards does

Kestrel Ridge Design wants the client's signature first on its $18,400 statement of work. The app sends the document to Marisol Quintero at Tamsin Orchards and holds the countersignature request. When Marisol signs, the app sends it on to the agency principal, Dov Albrecht, to countersign.
fields.tab_content_2:
Three partners, one consent, signed in any order

Three partners at Linnet Hollow Partners must sign the same consent, and none needs to wait for another. The app sends it to all three at the same time: Oluwaseun Brandt, Henrike Salo, and Tavish Moreau. Two of the three have signed. The consent stays open until Tavish signs, because only 3 of 3 marks it complete.
fields.tab_content_3:
Reminders on day 3 and day 7, closed on day 14

Joelle Varga sent the service agreement to Ivo Okafor at Halvard Marine Supply on November 2, and he has not opened it. The app reminds him on day 3 and day 7, and copies Joelle on the second reminder so she can call him. On day 14, November 16, the link closes. Joelle then decides whether to resend.
fields.tab_content_4:
A signed lease lands in the customer's folder

Pellucid Dental's equipment lease needs two signatures: the owner, Rosalind Achterberg, and your leasing manager, Kwame Ostrowski. When Kwame signs, the app saves 2026-11-12 Pellucid lease.pdf in the Pellucid Dental folder, attaches the file to the customer record, and emails a copy to both signers.

fields.howto_title: How to Create an E-Signature Workflow
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to set up an e-signature workflow that gets each document signed and filed, then build it with Emergent.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 List what you send for signature
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Decide the order for each document
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Set reminders and a closing day
fields.howto_step_1_des: List every document your team sent for signature last quarter, such as statements of work, leases, and partner consents. Note who signed each one and how many days the last signature took to arrive.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Decide whether each document's signers go in turn or sign at the same time. Put a signer in order only when their signature depends on an earlier one, such as an agency countersigning after its client.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Mark which fields belong to which signer: the client fills in the billing contact, and the owner initials the payment schedule. Each signer then sees only the fields that are theirs to complete.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Choose the reminder days and the day the link closes. Copy the sender on the last reminder: it gives a person time to call the signer before the link expires.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Name the folder and the record each signed copy belongs in, with a file name that starts with the date. Decide who gets a copy by email once the last signer signs.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Write the rules from the steps above as plain sentences and give them to Emergent. It turns them into a working app, and you change any rule later by prompting again.
fields.howto_step_7_des: Send one test document to two colleagues, one in each signing role, with the reminder days shortened to minutes. Have one colleague ignore it, and watch each reminder arrive and the link close.

faq_plan.a: An e-signature workflow is the set of rules a document follows once it is ready to sign: who signs it, in what order, how a quiet signer is chased, and where the signed copy is filed. It starts after any internal review and ends when the last signer has signed and the copy is stored.

faq_plan.q: How do I create an e-signature workflow?
faq_plan.a: List the documents you send for signature and who signs each, then describe the rules to Emergent's AI automation builder in plain English. It builds the app that sends each request and keeps the signing record. Start with the document you send most often, and add the others once its rules work.

faq_plan.q: What should an e-signature workflow record when someone signs?
faq_plan.a: Record who signed, when, and the exact version they saw. The federal ESIGN Act defines an electronic signature as a sound, symbol, or process attached to a record and "executed or adopted by a person with the intent to sign the record" (15 U.S.C. 7006). Make that intent plain with a button that says Sign. Ask your counsel what else your documents need.

faq_plan.q: Which documents need an e-signature workflow rather than an approval step?
faq_plan.a: Documents an outside party has to agree to need signatures: a statement of work, a lease, or a partner consent. Work your team only reviews before it goes out, such as a blog post or an ad, needs sign-off rather than a signature and belongs in a content approval workflow. Keeping the two apart means the signing record holds signatures only.

faq_plan.q: How many reminders should an e-signature workflow send before the link closes?
faq_plan.a: Two is a sensible default: one a few days after sending and one a few days before the link closes. After the second, change the channel rather than sending a third email: have the sender call or message the signer. The apps Emergent builds have no task cap, so the number of reminders is yours to set.

faq_plan.q: Can an e-signature workflow use the signing tool my team already pays for?
faq_plan.a: Yes, if that tool has an API. The app Emergent builds can connect to it, send each request through it, and read back when a signer has signed. The signing order, reminders, and filing then sit in the app, while your current tool collects the signatures.

faq_plan.q: Should an e-signature workflow wait for internal approval before sending?
faq_plan.a: Yes, for any document whose terms your team sets, such as pricing or a discount. Run it through your approval workflow first, and start the signature request only when the last approver says yes. The signer then receives the version your team agreed on, not one someone is still editing.

faq_plan.q: Where should an e-signature workflow store signed copies?
faq_plan.a: Store each signed copy in the customer's folder, named with the signing date first. Some laws require a record of a transaction in or affecting interstate or foreign commerce to be kept. The ESIGN Act lets an electronic record meet that rule if it stays accurate and accessible to everyone entitled to it for the period required. Ask counsel how long to keep each document type.

faq_plan.q: What should happen when a signer declines in an e-signature workflow?
faq_plan.a: The request should stop and go back to the sender with the signer's reason. Give the signing page a Decline button that asks why, cancel the reminders still queued, and mark the document declined on the board. If the fix is a changed term, send the new version as a fresh request and close the old link.

faq_plan.q: What should happen after the last signature in an e-signature workflow?
faq_plan.a: Filing the copy is the minimum, and the last signature can also start the work the document allows. A signed statement of work can open the project, and a signed vendor agreement can create the spend record your budget approval workflow tracks against. Tie each of those rules to the last signature, never the first.

plan.angle: The top 10 are e-signature vendors and glossary pages that list the same generic stages (create, send, sign, store) without showing a single rule. This page shows the four rules a builder actually writes into an e-signature workflow, each drawn as a working screen: a signing order that holds the agency's countersignature until the client signs, three partners who sign the same consent at once, a reminder schedule with an expiry date for a signer who goes quiet, and the signed copy named and filed in the customer's folder. Who approves a contract belongs to the contract approval page and document review to the document approval page; this page starts once a document is ready to sign.
